newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday, with many investors still staying on the sidelines due to an unclear short-term trend, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,140 yuan ($2,425) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at 20,200 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,210 and a low of 20,110.
October fell 20 to 20,680 yuan. November and December closed unchanged at 20,450 and 20,200 respectively. February rose 50 to 20,150 and March 40 to 20,200.
Combined volume fell to 27,340 tonnes from 58,540.
Copper opened mixed and all the contracts moved in a narrow range of 100 yuan for most of the session.
Traders said both long and short position holders stayed on the sidelines due to an unclear short-term market trend.
"Short position holders were not interested in building new short positions at low levels and institutional buyers were unwilling to lift prices without market-moving news," one trader said.
Traders said institutions would support copper above the 20,000-yuan level in the short term unless there was major negative news.

"Despite poor fundamentals, speculative sellers are willing to offset short positions above the key support of 20,000 yuan," a second trader said. Analysts expect copper to test the 20,000-yuan level in the short term.
Aluminium ended mixed in slow trading. October rose 50 to 14,050 yuan and November fell 100 to 14,050.
Combined volume fell to 300 tonnes from 1,150.
